correctness.rationale: The exact eleven-vertex graph and disconnected-subset face predicate are reconstructed twice independently on every one of the 2047 nonempty vertex subsets. The finite matching includes all simplices, and the complete reversed Hasse digraph is acyclic at each level. Exact signed gradient-path reduction yields a 3x3 matrix with determinant of absolute value 2 and a unit 2x2 minor for k=3, so the integral Smith form is (1,1,2). The k=4,5,6 matrices have ranks 3,2,1 and unit rank minors, respectively. Direct independent mod-two simplicial homology matches every resulting integral group via universal coefficients. Forman matching equivalence plus classification of attaching maps from S^d to wedges of S^d for d>=3 yields the claimed integral homotopy types. The verifier is embedded and re-executable without packages.

originality.rationale: The foundational 2023 source implies only the k=2 case, explicitly credited. The new Moore-space stage and remaining mixed sphere-wedge stages are not covered by the inspected family theorems; a later general reconstruction paper makes no such homotopy determination. The Grötzsch graph violates all square-free and edge-disjoint-square hypotheses. Direct searches of indexed scientific records and accessible ledger claims found no theorem implying the exact stages, though unindexed equivalence remains possible.

value.rationale: The smallest triangle-free four-chromatic graph is the canonical first Mycielski obstruction; its ordinary cut filtration is a mathematically natural whole object, not an arbitrary graph/parameter slice. The k=3 stage has a nontrivial degree-two Moore attaching map and integral two-torsion, unlike the sphere-wedge conclusions for graphs without overlapping four-cycles; k=4 and k=5 show mixed-dimensional integral sphere wedges. Determining all levels gives a structural test case for the boundary of available topological cut-complex classifications. No family-wide theorem is inferred.
